topic.raw_topic: How emoji became a universal language

source_documents.title: Emoji
source_documents.content_text: Emoji are pictograms, logograms, ideograms, and smileys used in electronic messages and web pages. The emoji was created in 1999 by Japanese artist Shigetaka Kurita, who was working for the mobile carrier NTT DoCoMo. The word emoji comes from Japanese e (picture) + moji (character). It is a coincidence that it resembles the English words 'emotion' and 'emoticon'. The Unicode Consortium began incorporating emoji into the Unicode Standard in 2010. As of 2023, there are 3,782 emoji in the Unicode Standard.

source_documents.title: Emoji has nothing to do with 'emotion' — it's Japanese for 'picture character'
source_documents.content_text: Mind blown. I always assumed emoji was a combination of emotion + icon. Nope. It's literally just the Japanese words for picture (e) and character (moji). The resemblance to 'emotion' is pure coincidence. Kurita originally designed 176 emoji for Japanese flip phones and they were 12x12 pixel grids.
